paragraphs: Friend, here is what I think this mountain is about. Jesus lets three of His disciples see who He really is: radiant clothes, Moses and Elijah beside Him, and a voice from the cloud saying, "This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!" (Mark 9:7). Then the cloud lifts, and they see no one with them except Jesus (Mark 9:8). Moses and Elijah were great, but when the moment is over, Jesus is the One left standing, and He's the One God says to listen to.

Now look at what Jesus does next. Right after that glory, He talks about the Son of Man rising from the dead, and He asks why it is written that the Son of Man "must suffer many things and be rejected" (Mark 9:12). I bet that was hard to hear on the way down the mountain, and I think the three disciples were still sorting it out, since they were discussing what it meant to rise from the dead (Mark 9:10). The glory and the suffering are not two different stories. They belong to the same Jesus, and He is telling them ahead of time.

So what does that mean for you, baker? When you open the Word, the loudest voices around you will not always be the ones to follow, and God has already told us whose voice to follow. Listen to Jesus, even when what He says is harder than what you hoped to hear. And if you feel like Peter, with a mouth running way ahead of your brain, take heart. I have been there, and Jesus stays with you anyway.
